candidates.finding: Index S2=C uses a promise-tail queue around destructive shared workspace reset and collection. Predict a rejected or aborted request could release queue admission before full cleanup; falsify with native async interleaving and no-provider controls.
candidates.screening_result: The shipped inference routes await queue.run, whose promise tail awaits task completion and whose catch only heals later admission. The actual runInference finally awaits workspace.reset before task resolution. No native HTTP abort path that bypasses this queue was found in these supported routes; the predicted premature reset is not established. Source inspection only; no test or patch claimed.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C uses foreground TurnLock preempt signalling against background grant-child effect admission. Predict a foreground arrival between precheck and new effect could be missed; null if the supported safe-boundary contract already handles it.
candidates.screening_result: TurnLock announces foreground arrival before lock acquisition. Executor _precheck compares the preemption sequence/arrival mark and is repeated at authorization, first provider request, tool/report effects and terminal request. The source explicitly accepts a residual already-started in-flight effect; no unsupported claim of mid-effect cancellation is made. No source-anchored new admission edge warrants a patch. Inspection only.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C reserves declared overlapping child write scopes and provider slots, releasing on results. Predict failed launch/cancellation leaves a slot or scope orphan; null if all supported terminal paths run release.
candidates.screening_result: The current first-party extension releases the slot and declared scope on launch rejection, queued failure, queued cancellation and terminal watcher finalization. Parent shutdown can intentionally detach an independently running child rather than cancel it, a different documented scope boundary; it does not prove the prospectively predicted leaked reservation from a failed launch. No native regression or patch claimed.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C uses transactional task claims and dependent split-child ownership. Predict crash after claim leaves a child/parent stuck without safe recovery; falsify if first-party orphan handling or operator-mediated contract already closes it.
candidates.blocker: The source establishes transactional work claiming and parent/child split ownership, but no first-party post-crash orphan recovery contract, executable orphan fixture, or safe re-claim semantics was established. Need and counterfactual remain unresolved; no intervention is warranted or claimed.
candidates.screening_result: Source inspection only. A crash-after-claim issue is still a hypothesis, not an observed malfunction. No native test, patch, or external delivery.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C uses process-wide AndroidUseLease with idle expiry and touch on screen tool actions. Predict an in-flight long screen call crosses expiry and admits a competing session; falsify by fixed-clock real wrapper checks.
candidates.blocker: The lease TTL and finally-only touch make long-running screen actions a plausible competition window, but the independent host has no Java, Kotlin or Gradle runtime to execute a pinned first-party fixed-clock regression. Native runner unavailable (BLOCKED_INDEPENDENT_EXECUTION), and no first-party long-call lease policy/fixture was established. No verified benefit or patch is claimed.
candidates.screening_result: Inspection confirmed the lease touch timing; source-only hypothesis, with unresolved need and counterfactual. No artificial non-native positive test was substituted.

candidates.finding: Index S2=C uses versioned scoped lesson publication and CAS retry against concurrent postmortems. Predict a stale retry/retire after conflict could overwrite or resurrect newer lesson; null if all commits remain revision-fenced.
candidates.screening_result: Source apply_checked_batch enforces expected revisions inside the transaction. Retired entries retain tombstones and later mutations remain revision-fenced; stale retries cannot silently overwrite a newer revision on the inspected first-party path. No native regression or patch warranted, and no run claimed.
